newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA REPLACES ARMY CHIEF OF STAFF.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA REPLACES ARMY CHIEF OF STAFF.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet approved on Monday a defence minister's proposal to replace the chief of staff of the Bulgarian army following an introduction of a new rotation principle in the military forces' command.

"The motives for the replacement of general Tsvetan Tototmirov are in line with the introduction of a new principle to rotate heads of army, air and naval forces as a chief of the General Staff," Defence Minister Georgi Ananiev told reporters.

The presidency later issued a statement saying that President Petar Stoyanov, who is supreme commander of the armed forces, would sign a decree for the appointment of the head of the air forces, general Miho Mihov, as the chief of staff.
The statement also said Totomirov would be appointed as a national security secretary to the President.
Totomirov, chief of staff since 1994, and his successor Mihov are strong advocates of Bulgaria's bid for full NATO membership, officials said.
